options.option_text: Easily giving up
Holding firmly to something; persistent and determined
Quick to change opinions
Relating to tendons or muscles

questions.explanation: B is correct. TENACIOUS = not readily relinquishing a position; very persistent and determined. From Latin tenax (holding fast). 'A tenacious athlete who never gives up.' Synonym: persistent, dogged, relentless, resolute. Antonym: irresolute, yielding, wavering.

options.option_text: To make clear and transparent
To make unclear or confusing deliberately
To focus intensely on a task
To observe something closely

questions.explanation: B is correct. OBFUSCATE = to make unclear, confusing, or unintelligible; to obscure. 'Politicians often obfuscate the facts to avoid responsibility.' From Latin: ob (away) + fuscus (dark) = to darken. Synonym: obscure, muddle, confuse, bewilder. Antonym: clarify, elucidate, illuminate.

options.option_text: Acting rashly without thinking
Wary and unwilling to take risks; cautious and watchful
Having a wide field of vision
Extremely generous and open-handed

questions.explanation: B is correct. CIRCUMSPECT = wary and unwilling to take risks; careful about all circumstances. From Latin: circum (around) + specere (to look) = to look around carefully. 'A circumspect investor carefully evaluates all risks.' Synonym: cautious, prudent, wary, guarded. Antonym: reckless, impulsive.

options.option_text: Petty and unforgiving
Generous and forgiving, especially toward rivals or enemies
Extremely large in size
Loud and boastful about achievements

questions.explanation: B is correct. MAGNANIMOUS = very generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival. From Latin: magnus (great) + animus (soul) = great-souled. 'A magnanimous victor who praised his opponent's effort.' Synonym: generous, noble, gracious, bighearted. Antonym: petty, mean, ungenerous.

options.option_text: Calm and cooperative
Eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
Honest and sincere in dealing
Moving very slowly and laboriously

questions.explanation: B is correct. TRUCULENT = quick to argue or fight; aggressive, hostile. 'The truculent child argued with the teacher at every opportunity.' From Latin truculentus (fierce). Synonym: combative, pugnacious, belligerent, aggressive. Antonym: cooperative, peaceful, amenable, docile.

options.option_text: Using many words; wordy and long-winded
Using very few words; brief and concise in speech
Relating to lake regions and water bodies
Prone to exaggeration

questions.explanation: B is correct. LACONIC = using very few words; brief and to the point. From Laconia (Sparta) — Spartans were known for brief, pointed speech. 'A laconic reply: 'No.' Synonym: terse, succinct, pithy, monosyllabic. Antonym: verbose, garrulous, loquacious, long-winded.

options.option_text: Modest and understated in behaviour
Designed to impress others; showy and flashy display of wealth
Careful and thorough in work
Stubborn and inflexible in opinions

questions.explanation: B is correct. OSTENTATIOUS = characterised by vulgar or excessive display; designed to impress. 'His ostentatious lifestyle included a fleet of luxury cars.' Synonym: showy, gaudy, flashy, flamboyant, pretentious. Antonym: modest, understated, humble, simple.

options.option_text: Loyal and trustworthy
Deceitful and untrustworthy; guilty of betrayal
Extremely skilled and perfect in work
Taking great pleasure in little things

questions.explanation: B is correct. PERFIDIOUS = deceitful and untrustworthy; guilty of betrayal. From Latin: per (through) + fides (faith) = breaking faith. 'A perfidious ally who betrayed his allies to the enemy.' Synonym: treacherous, disloyal, traitorous, faithless. Antonym: loyal, faithful, trustworthy.

options.option_text: To speak clearly and directly
To use ambiguous language to conceal the truth or avoid commitment
To feel equal and fair towards all
To excite or provoke strong emotion

questions.explanation: B is correct. EQUIVOCATE = to use vague or ambiguous language to hide the truth or avoid making a commitment. 'The politician equivocated when asked about his stance on tax reform.' From Latin: aequi (equal) + vox (voice) = speaking with two equal voices. Synonym: prevaricate, hedge, waffle. Antonym: assert, state clearly, commit.

options.option_text: Preferring solitude and avoiding company
Fond of company; sociable and outgoing
Living in the wilderness away from civilization
Relating to agriculture and farming practices

questions.explanation: B is correct. GREGARIOUS = fond of the company of others; sociable. From Latin: grex (flock). Originally described animals that live in flocks/herds; now means socially outgoing. 'A gregarious person who thrives at parties.' Synonym: sociable, outgoing, extroverted, convivial. Antonym: solitary, reclusive, introverted.
